questions.question: What does TwoTower.encode_image return for eight image feature rows?
options: Eight class labels without embeddings
One unnormalized vector for the whole batch
Eight L2-normalized embedding vectors
A 2D image tensor with three channels
questions.explanation: The image projection maps each row to the embedding dimension and F.normalize scales each vector to unit length.

questions.question: What does clip_loss compare for a batch of N paired image and text embeddings?
options: Only image classification accuracy against pixel labels
Euclidean distance between raw input dimensions
The number of tokens in each prompt
Image-to-text and text-to-image cross-entropy with diagonal pair targets
questions.explanation: The similarity matrix is logit_scale*i@t.T; cross-entropy is computed on it and its transpose with targets arange(N).

questions.question: Why does zero_shot_classify use argmax of i@t.T?
options: Normalized image and class-text embeddings have cosine similarity equal to their dot product
The dot product is a probability that already sums to one
Argmax selects the text prompt with the longest name
The method compares image pixels to class IDs
questions.explanation: Both encoders return unit vectors, so their dot product is cosine similarity; the highest-scoring class prompt is selected.

questions.question: What role does logit_scale.exp() play in the TwoTower forward result?
options: It converts text embeddings back into token IDs
It supplies a positive temperature-like scale for the contrastive logits
It normalizes the batch dimension to one
It clips every similarity to zero
questions.explanation: The learned scalar is exponentiated to stay positive and multiply the image-text similarity matrix before cross-entropy.

questions.question: With eight unrelated random pairs, what rough loss does the code print as a sanity baseline?
options: Exactly zero, because random pairs are always correct
Around log(2), because there are only two towers
Around log(8), because there are eight possible text matches per image
Around 128, because image features have 128 inputs
questions.explanation: If every row is nearly indistinguishable, choosing one of eight pair positions gives a cross-entropy near log(8); the symmetric term has the same baseline.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using class_text_feats in zero-shot classification?
options: They replace the image encoder's weights at inference
They supply bounding boxes for each object
They determine the image resolution
They provide one text embedding per candidate class without task-specific classifier training
questions.explanation: The method compares an image embedding with the text embeddings of candidate class prompts and returns the highest-scoring class name.
